what_is_said: Agent N. Srikantha Sastry asked the Chief Secretary (3 Nov 1927) for military escort and police arrangements for the Jagadguru's visits from the Sankar Mutt, Bangalore, to receive bhiksha and padapuja at the Basavangudi bungalows of G. Srinivasa Iyer (Chief Court judge, 4 Nov) and N. Krishna Rao (Member of Council, 6 Nov), citing precedents of 1907 and 1911. The 1907 order (Muzrai Secretary, 16 May 1907) gave an escort of the strength used in 1895: 4 NCOs and 30 rank and file plus 6 NCOs and 24 rank and file with a full band 29 strong.
quote: I have the honour to inform that His Holiness Sri Jagadguru will be proceeding from Sankar Mutt at 9 A.M. toemorrow, Friday, the
notes: Precedents enclosed: Muzrai Secretary letter No. 5352 of 16 May 1907 and Secretary letter of 24 Jan 1911 (padapuja at D. Devaraja Urs bungalow). Order of Govt in the file not legible.

what_is_said: On the Jagadguru's arrival at Shimoga (10 Jan 1928) the Reception Committee claimed that he was entitled to an infantry Guard of Honour; the Deputy Commissioner, Shimoga, sought orders and the Mutt wired for a guard 'as on previous occasion'. Government allowed a guard if there was precedent; the DC traced G.O. No. 1760-64 of 13 Jan 1911 (guard of honour and military escort at Bangalore, and also at Shimoga in 1911) and the 2nd Battalion furnished a Guard of Honour and military escort for the procession in Shimoga town.
quote: Jagadguru of Sringeri Mutt, Mr. Raghavia, a leading - Advocate of Shimoga and Secretary of the Reception Com- mittee wrote to me on the %th stating that His Holiness is entitled to a Guard of Honour by the Infantry
notes: Catalogue dates 1927; correspondence is Jan 1928. Much of the OCR is newspaper-advertisement backing of telegram forms.

what_is_said: The Muzrai Commissioner (2 Nov 1927) recommended that Rs 500 (not the Rs 800 asked) be sanctioned from Muzrai funds, debited to the Sivaganga Mutt's funds, for the bhiksha and padapuja of the Sringeri Jagadguru during a two-day halt at Sivaganga on his return to Sringeri; the Sivaganga Mutt could not pay interest on loans already given.
quote: Jagaiguru of Sringeri intends making a stay of two days at Sivaganga on his way to Sringeri.
notes: Concerns the Sivaganga Mutt (a separate Smarta mutt under Muzrai education committee) hosting the Sringeri Swami; catalogue calls it a lease, but it is a loan/sanction. Approved by G.O. No. 720-21/Muz. 110-27-2 of Nov 1927 (cited in next file).

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner asked sanction for extra expenditure of Rs 51-2-6 beyond the Rs 500 sanctioned for the Sringeri Jagadguru's visit to Sivaganga (arrived 25 Nov 1927, received by the Deputy Commissioner, Bangalore). Of the Rs 500, Rs 300 was offered as padapuja and a silver tray with about Rs 100 presented; the Jagadguru examined the young Sivaganga Swami and suggested he study Vedanta at Sringeri under the Jagadguru.
quote: so fan. 31s Holiness further <u; {ested certain changes in the metnad of teeching “rich have alreadv been brought into efect.
notes: Catalogue gives Rs 57-2-6; OCR reads Rs.51-2-6. Report by D. Venkataramaiah, Sivaganga Matt Education Committee, 14 Dec 1927. Proposal that the Sivaganga Swami be kept at Sringeri for Vedanta under the Jagadguru.

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner recommends an extra Rs 4 a month for the personal expenses of the Swamigalu of the Sri Sivaganga Matha, on top of the Rs 8 a month in the existing scale. Not about the Sringeri Mutt.
quote: I have the honor to state that the Agent, Sri Sivaganga - Matha requests sanction to an extra sum of Rs.4/= per month for
notes: matha=other: Sivaganga Matha. Catalogue misreads it as Sringeri and gives Rs 2 p.m.; OCR has Rs 8/- per month as the existing allowance.

what_is_said: The Agent asked Government to reconsider the order of 28 Apr 1928 making Sringeri a minor municipality with its entire tax income devoted to municipal purposes, which took away the moiety of municipal collections that the Mutt had enjoyed under order No. 13801-4 of 13 Feb 1893 until 1917. He asked that the Mutt be relieved of its agreement to meet the cost of the Local Fund Dispensary at Sringeri; the file discusses the Mutt paying three-fourths of the dispensary cost and a revised share.
quote: Government having recognised the title of the Sringeri Kutt to a moiety of the entire collections of the Sringeri Munici- pality in their order No 13801-4/51-92 dated 13-2-1893
notes: The Jahgirdar (the Swami) refused in 1917 to give up the moiety. The final contribution ratio for the dispensary is not clear in the OCR.

what_is_said: Dispute over the Barr infantry guard attached for about 40 years to guard the Saradamba temple and the jewels given by the Mysore kings. The Mutt had paid Rs 56 a month, but G.O. of 2 Apr 1924 (confirmed 14 Jul/Aug 1924) required the full cost of Rs 120 a month from 1 Apr 1924, leaving arrears of Rs 3,190-5-0. The Agent asked for the guard free, citing a free Palace guard at the Parakala Mutt, Mysore. Government (Financial Secretary, 13 Dec 1928) refused to reopen the matter. It held that the Mutt was not liable for the guard that went with the Swami on tour (G.O. 857 of 19 Dec 1923: one Biradari of Silledars and an infantry guard) and set the Rs 756-6-0 due to the Mutt against its dues.
quote: About 40 years ago Government were pleased to sanction a Guard of Barr Infantry to safeguard the Saradamba Temple and
notes: The Parakala Mutt has a Palace Barr Pahare of 6 sepoys and 2 officers, not a military guard. A later letter says the enhanced contribution was ordered from January 1929.

what_is_said: The Kadur District Board resolved (2 Jan 1930) that it could not take over the Sringeri Jahagir roads on the Government grant of Rs 5,000 a year for communications, primary education and medical relief in the Jahagir. The Executive Engineer needed Rs 15,000 for initial special repairs and Rs 2,450 a year for road repairs, while the Board's total income from the Jahagir area would be about Rs 3,067.
quote: the grant of Rs 5,000/- to the District Board for meeting the charges in respect of communications, Primary Education, =
notes: Shows Jahgir services being shifted to the District Board around 1929-30.

what_is_said: Constitution of Sringeri town into a permanent (minor) municipality under the Mysore Municipal Regulation, 1929-30: draft proclamations and boundaries (the boundary runs to the southern corner of the Mutt compound). The Agent (3 May 1930) asked that paddy fields of about 55 acres, assessed at Rs 190, be excluded from the municipal area as Mutt land not handed over to the Municipality.
quote: area of about 55 acres assessed to Rs 190/. Revenue and as such it has nesesssrily to be excluded from the Municipal area since
notes: Linked to files on the Agent's powers over the municipality (1930-31).

what_is_said: A srimukha with prasadam received by the Dewan in the Sringeri Swami's name in 1929 was not sent by the Sringeri Mutt. The Agent of the Sringeri Jahgir said it probably came from the Kudli Mutt, which had begun to drop 'Kudli' and style itself 'Sringeri Mutt'. He suggested a communication be sent to the Kudli Mutt insisting that it keep the name 'Kudli Sringeri Mutt'.
quote: I writo to ocknowledgo rocoipt of your DO, letter, ho. 397 of tho 30th Ultimo addressed te His Holtwass Sri Ungndsuru, sad
notes: Important for the Sringeri/Kudli Sringeri rivalry: Kudli Mutt styling itself Sringeri Mutt (1929). Key sentence OCR is garbled: "Sutt fro. whien" etc.

what_is_said: Land acquisition (19 Feb 1929) for the restoration of the Herekere tank at 'Sringeri Chandamanahalli' village, Mulbagal taluk, Kolar District. Probably a homonymous village, not the Mutt (based on the catalogue description).
quote: (no legible text)
notes: No OCR on IA; from catalogue description. Likely irrelevant to the Mutt.

what_is_said: Agent N. Srikanta Sastry (16 Jun 1931) reported that the Jagadguru had appointed Rao Bahadur N.S. Nanjundaiya, pleader of Hassan, as Agent from 1 Jul 1931, and asked that all the powers of the present Agent under the Land Revenue Code, the Excise Regulation and the Municipal Regulation be conferred on him. A notification of 23 Jun 1931 had already given the Agent supervisory powers over the new Sringeri Municipality from 1 Aug 1931.
quote: Jagadguru has been pleased to appoint Rao Bahadur N,S,Nanjundayye, Esq., Pleader,Hassan, a8 Agent, Sringeri Mutt, with effect from
notes: Catalogue year 1930; correspondence 1931. The Agent exercises Deputy Commissioner-type powers under the LR Code and the Excise Regulation.

what_is_said: Bulletins (c. Nov 1930) on the health of the Swami (Chandrasekhara Bharati), who had a mental illness. He improved, had lucid intervals, read the Vivekachudamani, moved his lodging to Satchidananda Vilas across the river, and by late November was reported fully restored to normal health (Senior Surgeon to Chief Secretary).
quote: Jahagir reports in his letter dated 20%h Instant, that His Holiness has been completely restored to his normal health
notes: Topic coded succession as the health of the Swami bears on the succession; alternatively management.

what_is_said: In a srimukha of 22 Apr 1931 to the Maharaja, Chandrasekhara Bharati Swami nominated the brahmachari Srinivasa Sastry, son of Vedamurti (Bangalore) Rama Sastry, who had studied in the Mutt for a year, for sanyasa and eventual succession. G.O. No. 2505-17-Muz. 299-30-4 of 18 May 1931 approved the nomination on behalf of the Maharaja; no proclamation was issued because the peetha was not vacant. The Muzrai Commissioner and the DC, Kadur, attended the induction on 22 May 1931 and the boy was given the name Sri Abhinava Vidyatirtha, with a procession of both Swamis round the town.
quote: His Holiness Sree Chandrasekhara Bharathi Swamigalu of Sringeri Mutt has represented in his Srimukha dated 22nd April 1931, that he has found it desirable to
notes: Precedent check: no facilities were asked for or given in April 1912 when the present Swami took ashrama (Member N. Nanjundayya was present). Catalogue year 1930.

what_is_said: Agent N.S. Nanjundaiah asked (Aug 1931) that the Agent and the Deputy Amildar continue as President and Vice-President of the new Sringeri Municipal Council. Asked whether he would give up his Deputy Commissioner-like powers of control over the Council if made President, the Agent replied (Oct 1931) that the Jagadguru, as Jahgirdar, did not wish him to resign those powers. He would serve as President only while keeping them.
quote: His Holiness the Jagadguru Mahaswami- galavaru, the Jahgirdar, is of opinion that I should not agree to resign thése powers
notes: See next file: Government instead made the Deputy Amildar President.

what_is_said: Constitution of the Sringeri Municipal Council (12 members: 6 elected, 6 nominated including Jahagir officials; G.O. of 23 Jun 1931). Only four candidates stood and were declared elected. By notification the Deputy Amildar of the Sringeri Jahgir was made President and Honnavalli Anniah Heggade nominated Vice-President (late 1931).
quote: the Deputy Amildar of the Sringert Jahgir shall ho the President of the Sringeri Mimicipal Council,
notes: Elected included Javagal Naga Bhatta and Baggunji Lingiah Setty.

what_is_said: The Deputy Commissioner, Kadur (15 Feb 1932), recommended that Government sanction the Sringeri Municipal Council's resolution of 15 Mar 1931 to hold a weekly shandy every Monday in Sringeri (the Koppa shandy is on Sundays). No objections were received.

what_is_said: Request by the Sri Vyasaraja Swami Matt of Sosale (Madhva) to be treated as equal to the Sringeri Mutt in the grant of the first day's bhiksha (a State-funded honour). The OCR has only a Kannada petition and printed Kannada office forms (apparently a return-of-petition form listing defects such as unstamped or wrong form). What is said is based on the catalogue description; the outcome is not legible.
quote: (no legible text)
notes: Based on the catalogue description. The Kannada form text suggests the petition was returned for formal defects, but this is uncertain.

what_is_said: Agent's bulletins and reports (Oct 1931 to Jan 1932) on a relapse of the Senior Swami Chandrasekhara Bharati's 'old complaint of mental aberration' from 22 Oct 1931. He was calm with lucid intervals and gave an interview to M.S.M. Sharma of Madras. The Dewan (Mirza Ismail) asked that bulletins go direct to the Huzur Secretary.
quote: True. Vis FYolinecs has heen indisposed since 22na ultimo due to a relapse of his old complaint of mertal arerration end that after
notes: Shows the recurring illness that led to Government management in 1935.

what_is_said: Mysore Gazette, 28 May 1931: the third-class powers of the honorary special magistrates of the bench courts at Koppa and Sringeri (Sringeri: H. Anniah Heggade) withdrawn from 1 Jul 1931. The page also has cholera notices.
quote: the Third Class powers con- ferred on the undermentioned Honorary Spec at Magi:irates of the Bench Cours at Kopp and Sringeri are hereby withdrawn
notes: Irrelevant to the Mutt.

what_is_said: Gazette notice (25 Apr 1931, L 8759 ML 60-30-18) extending the term of the reconstituted Sringeri Municipal Board (based on the catalogue description).
quote: (no legible text)
notes: No OCR on IA; from catalogue description. The extension notification No. 8759 is cited in file 16 (term to 31 Oct 1931).

what_is_said: The Comptroller (1934) asked that the Sringeri Municipality open an account in the Government Treasury at Koppa. It was transacting all its business in the Jahagir Treasury, so Government dues (Local Fund Dispensary contributions, pension contributions) could not be enforced, and the Jahgir paid it no interest. The audit of 9-10 Mar 1934 found careless accounts under President K. Subramanya Sastry, Deputy Amildar.
quote: loth tarch 1934, I have the honor to state that tre tunticipality is at present transacting all its business in the Jaharir Treasury
notes: Quote is fewer than 12 words because of OCR; the surrounding text is garbled. Catalogue year 1933; correspondence 1934.

what_is_said: Senior Surgeon's reports (1933) on the health of the Senior Jagadguru: in August he was 'perturbed in mind again and subject to hallucinations' and violent. By 10 Sep 1933 he was improving with long lucid intervals but not free from hallucinations. The reports were put before the Maharaja.
quote: Assistant Surgeon, Sringeri, to say that His Holiness the Senior Swami is perturbed in nind again and subject to hel- lucinations.

what_is_said: Final Notes of 9 Nov 1933 and Sept 1934. The Senior Swami was mentally ill, the junior Swami had fever, and Agent N.S. Nanjundaiya wanted to resign. Ex-Agent Srikanta Sastri proposed that the Senior Swami go to Kaladi, that the junior Swami be kept at the Sankaralaya, Mysore, for five years of education, and that a new Agent be appointed. Government considered taking over the Jahgir under s.25 of the Muzrai Regulation but deferred to the Swami. After the Muzrai Commissioner (N. Madhava Rao) visited on 17-18 Aug 1934, Government Order of 17 Sep 1934 appointed C. Rama Rao, Amildar of Kadur, as 'Agent' for two years ('Administrator' rejected). He had Deputy Commissioner powers under s.99 of the LR Code and pensionary contribution was to be recovered. Government stated that 'the responsibility for the management vests with the Swamigalu and not with Government'.
quote: would like to make it clear that the responsibility for the management vests with the Swamigalu end not with Government
notes: Srikanta Sastri went to South India in 1934 to manage the Mutt properties there. K. Gundu Rao was also proposed in 1933. This is the precursor of the 1935 takeover.

what_is_said: Gazette notice of G.O. MUZ 2505-17 / MUZ 299-30-4: induction of brahmachari Srinivasa Sastri into the sanyasasrama of the Sringeri Mutt (based on the catalogue description).
quote: (no legible text)
notes: No OCR on IA. The catalogue dates it 18 May 1934, but the G.O. number matches the order of 18 May 1931 (file 14), so the year is probably 1931.

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner forwards (Mar 1936) the Officer-in-Charge's note on the maṭh's properties outside Mysore, "the bulk" in Madras Presidency, earlier managed by N. Srikantha Sastry under a special power of attorney of 5-4-1934: Tavatherandal inam (719 acres, kist Rs 164) for Candramaulīśvara; five Ramnad villages gifted by Bhaskara Sethupathi (1864/1894) for Śāradā-Candramaulīśvara; Sendanadi and two Tirupattur houses taken by mortgage (22-6-1934) from the defaulting local agent Subramanya Iyer for ~Rs 14,000; 11½/28 shares of Pudurvalasai bought from Maddur Chandramouliswara Sastri for a Rs 27,000 loan from the Kaladi Veda Pathasala fund; a maṭh and three houses at Rameswaram (one bought for Rs 4,000); a maṭh at Madura; Travancore cash grant Rs 494 a year plus 26 acres at Kaladi; Coimbatore lands at Avanasi (179 acres, leased 99 years for Rs 1,400), Pudukarai/Savandapur (bought for a Rs 20,000 loan), Perumughai (mortgaged for Rs 15,000+1,200), Kadathur/Karatholam (for a Rs 45,000 loan to K. Narayana Sastry), Kangayam; Chinnamapet inam village (Tiruttani); and in Bombay/States Gangapur (Gadag, gift of Saka 1652), Paravi Basapur (gift of 1785-86), Pimpalgaon (Rahuri, gift of Madaji Sindia 1793-94, income made over to the Nasik maṭh), Gajendragad/Hebballi and Konanur (Ramdurg). Srikanta Sastry's letter of 17-3-1936 lists his six acts (Gobichettipalayam purchase for Rs 20,000; Rs 19,250 hypothecation from Akhilandammal; Benares/Rameswaram compromise; Rs 29,160 purchase from Laxmiammal; Sendanadi mortgage; Coimbatore suit O.S. 218/1935). Officer-in-Charge Y. Srikantaiya toured Madura/Ramnad (1936) and again 1938-39: income from Ramnad villages fell from >Rs 10,000 to negligible, agent irregular, accounts proposed to be controlled from Sringeri; Government obtained a general power of attorney from the Swami (7 May 1936).
quote: The Mutt owns extensive properties in the Madras and Bombay Presidencies and in some Native States. The bulk of the properties are in the Nadras Presidency.
notes: Long file 1936-39 (catalogue year 1935). Includes full text of the Swami's Special Power of Attorney to N. Srikantha Sastry (5-4-1934), revoking pro tanto N. S. Nanjundiah's general PoA of 5-7-1931. Branch maṭhs "managed by the local people by means of subscription" — list referred to but not legible. Figures for some acreages garbled (e.g. Pudurvalasai loan given as Rs 27,000 in one note and Rs 29,900 in another). Honorary Agent suggested entrusting the Pannandai division villages to the Raja of Ramnad (1939). Links: n=29, 43, 45, 48, 51, 52.

what_is_said: Final Note of the First Member of Council: the Swami (Candraśekhara Bhāratī) again ill and "mentally affected"; lending a Government officer to work under the maṭh (orders of 9-11-1933 and 30-8-1934) is unsatisfactory. With the Dewan's concurrence and the Maharaja's sanction, Government order (30 Jan 1936) takes the Sringeri Mutt with all its endowments and properties under Government management under Sec. 25(3) of the Mysore Religious and Charitable Institutions Regulation VII of 1927 for two years in the first instance; Agent C. Rama Rao reverted, Y. Srikantaiya appointed Officer-in-Charge under the Deputy Commissioner, Kadur. The Junior Swami to be moved to Bangalore/Mysore for study; the Muzrai Commissioner advised waiting (Feb 1936) as the Senior Swami asks for him in lucid intervals.
quote: Government are pleased to direct that the Sringeri Mutt with all its endow- ments and properties be taken over under their management under Section 25(3) of the Mysore Religious and Charitable Institutions Regulation VII of 1927 for a period of 2-years in the first instance.
notes: Catalogue year 1935; order issued 30-1-1936. Proposal had been considered in 1934 but held in abeyance "in deference to the wishes of the Swami". Consent of the Swami to be obtained on recovery. Links n=30, 35, 36, 37.

what_is_said: After the takeover the Muzrai Commissioner asks (Feb-Mar 1936) that Madras, Travancore, Bombay and the States (Ramdurg, Gajendragad) be notified through the Resident to give facilities to the Officer-in-Charge. A village-by-village list of Madras/Travancore properties with local managers is sent (May 1936). Bombay Government (7 May 1936) instructs the Commissioners of Central and Southern Divisions; Madras G.O. Ms. 1216 (4 Jun 1936) directs Collectors to help the local managers collect revenue. Travancore's annual varshasanam of Rs 495-1-5 (1936-37) is paid via K. Sambasiva Sastri, Curator, Oriental Manuscripts Library, Trivandrum (1937).
quote: the Mutt owns properties in the Rombay Presidency} and certain other Native States noted in the margin.
notes: Local managers named in list: S. Subramanya Iyer (Tirupattur), G. V. Ramakrishna Iyer (Gobichettipalayam), K. V. Krishnaswami Iyer (Kangayam), etc. Travancore payment = cash grant for Kaladi (cf. n=27).

what_is_said: Chief Secretary's note (Jan 1936): Agent C. Rama Rao reported the Swami "slightly indisposed" though other sources said the attack was serious and violent; Rama Rao judged weak, of doubtful straightforwardness, a local man who had "become all in all" in the maṭh; recommends Government take over the Jahgir under Sec. 25(3) and post an Assistant Commissioner-grade officer with Rs 100 local allowance; a separate Sarvadhikari for internal and religious matters. Government (G.O. 25-2-1936) sanction Rs 100 p.m. local allowance to Y. Srikantaiya, Officer-in-Charge, from maṭh funds.
quote: I think the continuance of Mr. Rama Rao in his presen position is fraught with serious danger, because he is a loc+1 mar w_t}
notes: Previous attacks lasted six to eight months. Cites D.O. of N. Madhava Rao (25-8-1934) that Rama Rao was to confine himself to secular affairs. Gives the reasoning for the takeover.

what_is_said: Bad roads to Sringeri: Government (Mar 1936) direct that road improvement be planned by the Officer-in-Charge with the PWD and carried out by the PWD, using the accumulated 75% of local cess made over to the Jahgir since 1932 (G.O. 26-10-1932), for the two years of Government management.
quote: I em to eda that this arreagement may be in force for the twe years during which ihe Management of the Mutt will be in the hands of the Government.

what_is_said: Per catalogue description only: question of preferring appeals regarding legacies left by the late Madapathi Venkateswara Rao Pantulu in favour of the branch Sringeri maṭhs at Benares and Rameswaram.
quote: (no legible text)
notes: No OCR file. Context from n=27: Srikanta Sastry obtained a razinama compromise decree in the Madras High Court appeal; the Rameswaram maṭha to get an annuity of Rs 1,985 plus Rs 3,500 lump sum for its building from the purchaser of the Pantulu estates; the Rameswaram maṭha was built at Pantulu's wish and an image of Śaṅkarācārya consecrated there.

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner approves (Mar 1936), and Government confirm, the Deputy Commissioner's advice that tenants of the Sringeri Jahgir may continue to pay kandayam in kind (paddy and areca) until things settle down; the Officer-in-Charge had sold about 600 maunds of areca at Rs 5-1-0 a maund.
quote: the practice hitherto in vogue in the Jahgir of receiving the kandayam due by the ryots in the shape of paddy and areca nuts may continue until things settle down
notes: Paddy received is used for daily consumption of the maṭh.

what_is_said: The maṭh owns inam forests in its inam villages (Agasavalli etc.) in Shimoga Taluk suffering from unauthorised felling and smuggling of timber and sandalwood; on the Officer-in-Charge's proposal, Government (1936) sanction a Forester (Rs 25, lent by the Forest Department) and a Guard (Rs 8) for four months from maṭh funds, under the Amildar of the Jahgir.
quote: Sri Sringeri mutt owns inam foresb in the inam villages, Agasavalli etc., in Shimoga Taluk
notes: Catalogue year 1935; correspondence Mar-May 1936.

what_is_said: Recovery of pension and leave contributions (Rs 72-8-0 p.m. from his next increment, pay Rs 290) for Officer-in-Charge Y. Srikantaiya is waived as a special case (1936) because "the finances of the Mutt are at a low ebb" owing to economic depression and low produce prices. The Comptroller cites a 1910 precedent waiving contributions for Barr sepoys lent to the Sringeri and Raghavendraswami maṭhs.
quote: As the finances of the Mutt are at a low ebb and it is not ljykely that the collections from the endowed villages will come yp to expectations owing to present economic depression
notes: Total emoluments of the Officer-in-Charge Rs 300 a month. Link n=56 (waiver continued 1938).

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner visited Sringeri (6-8 Apr 1936): the recovered Senior Swami was satisfied with Government management, had himself been thinking of asking for it, was dissatisfied with C. Rama Rao, and said money had to be borrowed even for normal services; he asked only that internal arrangements and services not be disturbed. The Junior Swami had been drawn into an agitation against the takeover by local people including Rama Rao; both Swamis agreed he should complete his studies away from Sringeri. He left Sringeri on 21 Jun 1936 for the Shankara Mutt, Bangalore; Government sanction an establishment (teacher, manager, attendants, two student stipends) costing Rs 189 p.m. from the maṭh's closing balance (1936-37 budget surplus est. Rs 10,292).
quote: The Junior Swamigalu was drawn into this agitation by certain local people including Mr. C. Rama Rao, the Agent of the Mutt.
notes: Deputy Commissioner noted the takeover was legal only during the Swami's disability (Sec. 25 proviso) so his consent was needed after recovery. Plan first for Mysore Abhinava Shankaralaya, finally Bangalore. Link n=57 (return 1937).

The Officer-in-Charge and Deputy Commissioner asked for Rs 60,000 over 15 years; the Muzrai Commissioner recommended Rs 75,000 at 5% repayable in ten annual instalments adjusted from the annual sayer compensation of Rs 15,000, financed by selling 5% Mysore Loan Bonds of the General Muzrai Fund or Chattram Savings Fund; the Swami agreed; Financial Secretary, Second Member and the Maharaja sanctioned (Aug 1936).

what_is_said: C. Rama Rao, Amildar, Agent of the maṭh from Sep 1934 (two years, rank of Assistant Commissioner), retired 8 Apr 1936 amid complaints. Muzrai Commissioner proposed a 10% pension cut for life; First Member, Dewan and Second Member reduced it to six months (Sep 1936).

what_is_said: Final Note of the First Member of Council (agreed by the Dewan, submitted to the Maharaja): the Matt with all its endowments and properties, taken under Government management by G.O. 1028-30/Muz.174-35-2 of 30 Jan 1936 for two years with Asst Commissioner Y. Srikantiah as Officer-in-charge under the Deputy Commissioner, Kadur, is to remain under Government management until further orders, with Srikantiah continuing. The Muzrai Commissioner, after interviewing the Swami at Sringeri on 19-21 Nov 1937, reported that the Swami appreciated the 'quiet and efficient' management and himself asked for its continuance; the D.C. Kadur had noted the two-year period expired on 30 Jan 1938. The file also carries the 1959 order restoring the Matt's properties in and outside the State to the Matt's own management after the abolition of the Sringeri Jahgir.

notes: Management actually assumed on 17 Feb 1936 per Muzrai Commissioner's letter. Later papers: Srimukha of 23-3-1959 from the Jagadguru asking that, as the Sringeri Jahgir had been abolished from 1-4(?)-1959, management of properties in and outside the State be restored to the Mutt; sanctioned 1959. The Muzrai Commissioner adds 'It is necessary to continue the present management to further develop the resources and systematize the affairs.'
